text: . The gold rush continued for India at the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, as Indian athletes delivered a stellar performance on Day 13, clinching SIX gold medals – in Hockey, Boxing, Wrestling and Archery – in a spectacular display of skill, determination and sporting excellence.The Indian Women’s Hockey team clinched the gold medal, defeating China 1-nil in the closely fought final. Lalremsiami Hmarzote scored the decisive lone goal for India, while goalkeeper Savita Punia produced a crucial save from a penalty stroke to preserve the lead and secure the gold medal. The victory marks India’s first women’s hockey gold at the Asian Games in 44 years, ending a long wait for the title.Earlier, Indian wrestler Sujeet Kalkal scripted a remarkable comeback to win the gold medal in the men’s 65-kilogram freestyle event.In Boxing, Parveen Hooda won the gold medal in the women’s 65kg category, defeating Chinese Taipei’s Nien-Chin Chen 3-2 in a split decision in the final. Ankush Panghal clinched the gold medal in the men’s 80-kilogram category, defeating South Korea’s Kim Minseong by a split decision, 4-0, in the final.India’s star woman boxer Lovlina Borgohain also clinched a gold medal in the 75kg category, defeating China’s Bao Ziyi by a unanimous 5-0 decision in the final.In Archery, the women’s recurve team created history by clinching its maiden Asian Games gold medal. The trio of Ankita Bhakat, Kirti Sharma and Kumkum Mohod defeated world champions South Korea 5-3 in a thrilling final.India also bagged silver in the mixed recurve team event. Kumkum Mohod and Dhiraj Bommadevara finished runners-up after going down 3-5 to China in a closely contested final.In Sepaktakraw, India secured the bronze medal in the men’s quadrant event.In Sailing, Nethra Kumanan clinched bronze in the women’s dinghy event.With these impressive performances, India has climbed to fifth position in the overall medal standings. The country’s medal tally has risen to 76, including 16 gold, 25 silver and 35 bronze medals.President Dropadi Murmu and Prime Minister Narendra Modi have congratulated medal winners.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is completing 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into creation of the post of Chief of Defence Staff.Earlier, India’s three armed services – Army, Navy and the Air Force – planned, trained, procured and advised the government separately. Proposals for greater jointness had been made repeatedly since the Kargil Review Committee of 1999 and the Group of Ministers that followed it, but no single officer held authority across all three services. On the 15th of August 2019, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, in his Independence Day address, announced the creation of the post of Chief of Defence Staff from the ramparts of the Red Fort. Prime Minister Modi said this will lead to better coordination among the three services.The Cabinet approved the decision in December 2019, along with a new Department of Military Affairs within the Ministry of Defence for the CDS to head.  Talking to Akashvani News, retired Lt General Sanjay Kulkarni said the appointment of CDS made it possible for the government to have one point of contact for advice on allmiltarymatters.After the formation of the post of CDS, all three forces have now got effective leadership at the top level.

. Union Home Minister Amit Shah has said that the government has achieved a historic milestone by securing the deportation of hardened narco-trafficking kingpin Navpreet Singh from Türkiye. In a social media post, Mr Shah said that Navpreet Singh continued to smuggle heroin and methamphetamine to India from Afghanistan by obtaining Turkish citizenship under the fake identity of Navab Virk.The Minister said that agencies tracked him down, ripping apart veil after veil to unmask his true identity, and secured his deportation. He said that today the narco-trafficking kingpin has been brought back to India and put behind bars in connection with cases involving drug trafficking and other crimes he is accused of. Congratulations to all the agencies for the success, he said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government is committed to destroying every narco-cartel before December 2029.

. The Indian community in the UAE marked Gandhi Jayanti with tributes to Mahatma Gandhi, remembering his enduring message of peace, harmony and non-violence. At the Indian Embassy in Abu Dhabi, Ambassador Dr Deepak Mittal and embassy officials paid floral tribute to Mahatma Gandhi, reaffirming his timeless message of peace and non-violence. Consul General Dr E. Vishnu Vardhan Reddy, along with officials, paid floral homage to the bust of Mahatma Gandhi at the Consulate premises.Young Indian students from a music school in the UAE also paid homage to Mahatma Gandhi with a soulful rendition of ‘Vaishnav Jan To’ in Arabic and Hindi, reflecting the universal appeal of Mahatma Gandhi’s message of peace and harmony.

The National Statistics Office (NSO), is conducting the Forward-Looking Survey on Private Corporate Sector CAPEX Investment Intentions (CAPEX 2026) during the period of October to December 2026.The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation said that the survey is aimed at generating comprehensive and timely information on capital expenditure undertaken and planned by large private corporate sector enterprises. The Ministry added that the survey will provide important inputs for understanding emerging investment trends in the Indian economy.The primary objective of the CAPEX Survey is to collect information on capital expenditure undertaken in the recent financial years , provisional capital expenditure in the current financial year and investment intentions for the forthcoming financial year.The Ministry has appealed all the selected private corporate sector enterprises to extend their full cooperation and participate actively in the CAPEX 2026 Survey.

. Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has said the Global Horticulture Hub will strengthen the horticulture sector and create better opportunities for farmers in the Rayalaseema region of Andhra Pradesh.Ms. Sitharaman laid the foundation stone for the Rayalaseema Global Horticulture Hub project and the Indian School of Agriculture at Madanapalle in Annamayya district yesterday. Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu and Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan were present on the occasion.Speaking at the event, the Finance Minister said, the Centre and the State are working together to develop Andhra Pradesh as a major horticulture centre. She stressed the need for better water management, modern technology and infrastructure to support farmers and improve their incomes.The Finance Minister highlighted Central Government schemes, including PM-KISAN, crop insurance and PM-KUSUM. She also said climate-resilient crop varieties and solar-powered farm pumps are being promoted. The Union Minister said the Indian School of Agriculture will help farmers adopt modern technology, scientific methods and research. She expressed hope that the institution will develop into a world-class centre.The Global Horticulture Hub will cover ten districts and promote crops including mango, banana, tomato and pomegranate. The project will be implemented in three phases, with an estimated investment of about one lakh crore rupees.

Indian athletes continued their strong performance at the ongoing Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, winning several medals across multiple sporting events today.In Boxing, Lovlina Borgohain clinched a historic gold medal in the women’s 75kg category, defeating China’s Bao Ziyi by a unanimous 5-nil decision in the final. It is India’s second gold medal in women’s boxing at the Asian Games, following Mary Kom’s gold in 2014.Earlier, India’s women’s recurve archery team created history by winning its maiden Asian Games gold medal. The trio of Ankita Bhakat, Kirti Sharma and Kumkum Mohod defeated world champions South Korea 5-3 in a thrilling final. India won silver in men’s recurve archery team event.The Men’s team, comprising of Dhiraj Bommadevara, Yashdeep Sanjay Bhoge and Neeraj Chauhan, settled for silver after loosing 1-5 to South Korea in the final.India also secured a silver medal in the mixed recurve team archery event. The Indian duo of Kumkum Mohod and Dhiraj Bommadevara finished runners-up after losing 3-5 to China in a closely contested final. India also won a bronze medal in Sepaktakraw at the Asian Games today. The Indian men’s quadrant team lost 0-2 to Japan in the semi-final to secure the bronze medal.In sailing, Nethra Kumanan won the bronze medal in the women’s dinghy event. The 29-year-old Indian sailor finished third with overall 14 points.With these performances, India climbed to sixth position in the overall medal standings. The country’s medal tally rose to 72 medals, comprising 12 gold, 25 silver and 35 bronze.President Droupadi Murmu has congratulated Lovlina Borgohain on winning the gold medal in the Women’s 75kg Boxing event at the Asian Games 2026. In a social media post, President Murmu said that her strength, precision and determination in the ring have brought immense pride to the country.The President said that winning the Gold Medal on her birthday makes the occasion even more special. The President also congratulated Ankita Bhakat, Kumkum Anil Mohod and Kirti on winning the first-ever Gold Medal in the Recurve Women’s Team event in Archery at the Asian Games 2026.She also congratulated Dhiraj Bommadevara and Kumkum Anil Mohod on winning the Silver Medal in the Recurve Mixed Team event in Archery at the Asian Games 2026. The President said that it is a historic achievement, as your outstanding performance brings India its first-ever Silver Medal in this event.Prime Minister Narendra Modi has congratulated Ankita Bhakat, Kumkum Anil Mohod and Kirti on winning India’s first-ever Gold Medal in the Women’s Recurve Team event at the Asian Games. In a social media post, Mr Modi said that their composure and precision in a closely fought final were remarkable. He added that this landmark victory will inspire countless young archers across the country.The Prime Minister also congratulated Dhiraj Bommadevara and Kumkum Anil Mohod on winning the Silver Medal in the Recurve Mixed Team event at the Asian Games. He said that they displayed remarkable skill and zeal, giving the nation the first-ever Silver in this event at the Asian Games.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red colour warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall with isolated extremely heavy rainfall over Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand tomorrow. According to IMD, heavy to very heavy rainfall is likely over Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh tomorrow. The districts that are likely to receive heavy rainfall include Rampur, Pilibhit, Bareilly, Shahjahanpur and Bahraich. Meanwhile, districts of Madhya Pradesh which are expected to receive rainfall include Satna, Chhatarpur, Tikamgarh and Niwari.IMD said that the line of withdrawal of Southwest Monsoon continues to pass through Gurdaspur, Chandigarh, Muzaffarnagar, Aligarh, Dholpur, Udaipur, Deesa and Naliya.The Met Department has also predicted heavy rainfall over Delhi, Haryana, Chandigarh, Bihar, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Odisha, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim for the day. Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty windsare expectedto prevail over Punjab, Madhya Pradesh, Vidarbha, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Mahe, Telangana, Andaman and Nicobar Islands and parts of Northeast during the next two days.Meanwhile, parts of Delhi are expected to witness light to moderate rainfall tomorrow.

. Today is World Suicide Prevention Day. The day is observed worldwide to raise awareness about suicide prevention and the importance of mental health.The occasion reminds us that people facing emotional distress or difficult circumstances need timely support, understanding and appropriate care. Experts emphasise that listening to someone with patience and without judgement can encourage them to seek help and support.On this Day, people are encouraged to remain attentive to the emotional well-being of those around them and, when required, guide them towards family members, trusted persons or mental health professionals.

The ongoing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has claimed more than 4,000 lives, with health authorities reporting 4,018 deaths among 8,300 confirmed cases across seven provinces. The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention has warned that a recent decline in reported cases may reflect gaps in disease surveillance rather than a sustained reduction in transmission.According to the Congolese Health Ministry, 2,162 patients have recovered and the case fatality rate stands at 48.4 per cent.Africa CDC said the outbreak has spread from three health zones in mid-May to 63 health zones across seven provinces, with 45 health zones still reporting active transmission. It cautioned against interpreting the recent decline in reported cases as a sign that the outbreak is under control.International medical charity Médecins Sans Frontières has also warned that the actual death toll could be higher due to gaps in surveillance and case detection.Insecurity and community resistance in several areas have hampered surveillance and response efforts, raising concerns that some infections may be going undetected.

. The 5th Kautilya Economic Conclave will be held from this Saturday in New Delhi, under the theme of ‘Resilience in an Age of Flux’. The Ministry of Finance said that the three-day gathering will bring together more than 180 policymakers, economists, academics, financial experts and international thought leaders, including over 80 international participants from around 30 countries.The Ministry added that the Conclave will feature plenary sessions, interactive parallel sessions and roundtables. The roundtables will focus on issues including attracting foreign direct investment and mobilising domestic capital for long-term investment. The Ministry said that these roundtables will provide opportunities for more focused exchanges among policymakers, economists, investors and practitioners.Vice President C P Radhakrishnan will deliver the inaugural address on the first day of the conclave. The conclave will also witness addresses from Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar and other Union Ministers. The Ministry informed that the conclave will also feature a special address by the Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), Sanjay Malhotra.

The second edition of the India Art, Architecture and Design Biennale (IAADB) will be held from 4th December 2026 to 21st March 2027 in New Delhi.The theme of this 108-day Biennale is ‘Tat Tvam Asi – Reconnecting in an Age of Distraction’. Talking exclusively to Akashvani News, Secretary of the Ministry of Culture, Vivek Aggarwal said that, the Biennale will feature art installations at iconic heritage sites of the National Capital, including Purana Qila, Red Fort, Safdarjung Tomb, Qutub Minar, Qila Rai Pithora and Lodhi Garden. He said that the theme of this year’s Biennale directly takes inspiration from India’s ancient traditions and spiritual thought, which emphasize self-introspection and the unity of the individual with the larger universal consciousness.Mr Aggarwal said that the Ministry aims to take IAADB to a global level by encouraging participation from international pavilions and artists, Indian states and the private sector.Speaking about the cultural diplomacy of India, He said that cultural exchange is an important component of cultural diplomacy and the country’s soft power. Mr Aggarwal added that participation of foreign countries will provide an opportunity for Indian and international audiences to experience diverse art forms and will help position the Biennale on the global cultural calendar.Underlining the importance of Art and Design students in this Biennale, He said that the Ministry plans to involve students, particularly those pursuing art and design, in various activities associated with the Biennale, providing them opportunities to engage with artists and the wider creative ecosystem.The second edition of the India Art, Architecture & Design Biennale 2026 is the largest platform which offers artists, curators, galleries, corporates, architects, designers, cultural institutions and other stakeholders a chance to connect with culture and the creative world. This edition is conceived not as a single exhibition in a single location but as a city-wide cultural platform. Visitors will have an opportunity to experience the historical monuments along with contemporary art installations.

Several Indian diplomatic missions across the world today marked Mahatma Gandhi’s birth anniversary by paying floral tributes and recalling his timeless ideals of truth, non-violence and peace.Marking Gandhi Jayanti and the International Day of Non-Violence, the Indian High Commission in Australia offered a floral tribute at the Mahatma Gandhi Statue at Glebe Park in Canberra.Additionally, Indian Ambassador to Japan Nagma Mallick, along with Edogawa Ward officials and members of the Indian community, laid flowers at Mahatma Gandhi’s statue in Tokyo, while reflecting on his life and achievements.In New Zealand, Indian High Commissioner Muanpuii Saiawi, along with other dignitaries, paid tribute to Gandhi, reflecting on his life, teachings and their relevance in today’s world.Furthermore, in Cambodia, Indian Ambassador Vanlalvawna Bawitlung, along with Embassy officials and members of the Indian diaspora, paid floral tributes at Gandhi’s bust, honouring his timeless ideals of peace, truth and non-violence.Meanwhile, Norwegian Ambassador to India May-Elin Stener recalled her visit to Sabarmati Ashram and highlighted the enduring relevance of Gandhi’s message.In a social media post, Stener said that Gandhiji’s message continues to inspire people even today.Indian High Commissioner to Bangladesh, Dinesh Trivedi, today extended his warm greetings to everyone on the occasion of the birth anniversaries of Mahatma Gandhi and former Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri.He said that former Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri gave the slogan “Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan.” In today’s era, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said, “Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan, Jai Vigyan, Jai Anusandhan.” He further said that Mahatma Gandhi’s message of non-violence is particularly important today.Violence has increased across the world, and in such circumstances, Gandhiji’s message of non-violence and brotherhood becomes even more relevant.He said that even after so many years, Mahatma Gandhi remains loved by people across the world because his message will always remain relevant to humanity. He prayed that Mahatma Gandhi’s dream of Ram Rajya may be established not only in Hindustan but across the entire world.

The Group of Seven (G7) nations have agreed to release 100 million barrels of oil over four months in an effort to ease soaring fuel prices, with a substantial release of diesel planned in the first 20 days. The decision came as diesel prices in the United States climbed to record levels, adding pressure on President Donald Trump and his administration ahead of November’s midterm elections. Mr Trump said that European countries had agreed to release large quantities of diesel from their stocks and that the process would begin “immediately.”The announcement followed an overnight conversation between Trump and French President Emmanuel Macron. According to a statement issued by France after the meeting, the International Energy Agency (IEA) will coordinate the release. The G7 and partner countries will make a coordinated release of 100 million barrels over four months, with a substantial amount of diesel to be released during the first 20 days.The move comes as fuel prices have surged in the United States and other countries amid the eight-month-long war involving Iran. US diesel prices have risen sharply in recent weeks. The national average stood at 6.37 dollar per gallon on Friday, according to AAA, after reaching a record 6.52 dollar per gallon on September 22.

. G7 countries have agreed to release up to 100 million barrels of oil from strategic reserves over four months in a coordinated effort to bring down soaring energy prices, with a particular focus on diesel. The release will be coordinated by the International Energy Agency (IEA), with a substantial amount of diesel to be made available within the first 20 days. The G7 countries stated this in a statement released following a meeting of the bloc through video conference to discuss global diesel supply amid skyrocketing fuel prices and escalating trade friction between the United States and Europe.French President Emmanuel Macron, who currently holds the G7 presidency, said in a social media post that the countries had agreed to work in a coordinated manner to ease pressure on prices of petroleum products, particularly diesel. During the meeting, the G7 leaders also decided to make production more flexible to increase refinery output and pledged not to restrict trade in energy and oil products between partner countries.The move comes as US President Donald Trump threatened to halt American diesel exports if European countries do not release fuel from their strategic reserves. High domestic fuel costs are posing a significant political challenge for the Republican Party ahead of next month’s midterm congressional elections.European Commission officials strongly rejected the proposed U.S. diesel export ban, warning that it would damage trust in the US as a reliable partner.Global supply has tightened due to the ongoing US war with Iran. Additionally, Russia extended its diesel export ban following Ukrainian damage to its refineries, and Chinese refiners suspended exports to preserve domestic supplies.Meanwhile, average UK diesel prices have hit a record high, reaching 2 pounds a litre for the first time. However, UK Transport Minister Keir Mather has said Britain’s supply of diesel is robust and “resilient”, and the country has a wide range of sources.

. The country’s foreign exchange reserves declined by 18.3 billion US dollars (USD) to 747.5 billion US dollars during the week ended the 25th of September. According to Reserve Bank of India data, Foreign currency assets, the largest component of the reserves, dropped by 15.5 billion USD to 615.4 billion USD during the week. Gold reserves dropped by 2.5 billion USD to 108.7 billion US dollars. Special Drawing Rights fell by 97 million USD to 18.64 billion USD. The country’s reserve position with the International Monetary Fund dipped by 86 million to 4.8 billion USD.

. British-Indian chess prodigy Bodhana Sivanandan has been recognised by Guinness World Records as the youngest chess player to achieve the Woman Grandmaster (WGM) title. The 11-year-old London schoolgirl made history at the 46th Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, becoming the youngest player ever to earn the coveted WGM title.The achievement gives Bodhana three Guinness World Records titles. Her earlier records include being the youngest chess Woman International Master and the youngest female player to defeat a grandmaster in a chess tournament.Bodhana said the recognition is a huge honour and a morale boost, motivating her to continue improving and achieve more. Her journey into chess began at the age of five years and eight months, after she developed a fascination with the knight chess piece. She went on to win competitions by the age of six.Guinness World Records Editor-in-Chief Craig Glenday described Bodhana’s story as an inspiring example of how childhood curiosity and passion can lead to extraordinary achievements.

. India’s industrial output, as measured by the Index of Industrial Production (IIP), grew by 8% year-on-year in August this year. The latest data indicate that industrial activity continued to expand at a healthy pace, with the upward revision in July’s IIP growth to 7.4% from the earlier estimate of 6.7%.According to government data released today, electricity and gas supply recorded strong growth of 12.3% in August, while manufacturing, which carries the heaviest weight in the index, expanded by 9%. Water supply, sewerage and waste management also registered healthy growth of 6.3%. However, the mining sector remained a laggard, contracting by 5.6% during the period under review.

The Ministry of Education, in coordination with the External Affairs Ministry is organizing a two day Bharat Innovates Exposition from today at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi to showcase India’s Deep-Tech innovations as a lead up to and alongside the 18th BRICS Summit 2026. The Exposition is showcasing 37 India’s Deep-Tech startups and ventures alligning with the theme of India’s BRICS Chairship Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability. The event is providing participating innovators an opportunity to network with CEOs, investors, business leaders and industry representatives from BRICS member countries. Ministry of Eduaction said that the event will facilitate opportunities for Business to Business engagements, technology partnerships, investment discussions, business linkages and international market access.

The All India Consumer Products Federation and the All India Mobile Retailers Association have decided to withdraw their proposed call for a ‘No UPI Day’ on Friday.The decision was taken following a meeting between a delegation of around 20 senior trade leaders, led by BJP MP and Secretary General of the Confederation of All India Traders, Praveen Khandelwal, and Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman in New Delhi. During the meeting, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman assured the delegation that the government remains committed to promoting digital transactions while safeguarding the interests of all stakeholders.The trade leaders reiterated their full support for the Digital India mission and the success of UPI, which has emerged as a global model for digital payments. The delegation expressed confidence that continued dialogue between the government and trade bodies would help evolve a practical and sustainable framework to further strengthen India’s digital economy.

. The Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) hasissued redalert for extremely heavy rainfall over isolated places of Chhattisgarh, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Telangana for the next two days. The Met Department has predicted heavy rainfall over Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Meghalaya, Bihar, Jharkhand, Kerala, Maharashtra, West Bengal and Sikkim tomorrow. The weather department also forecast thunderstorms accompanied with highly gusty winds over Madhya Pradesh and Parts of North-East tomorrow.For Delhi, IMD said the national capital will witness mostly clear skies with no rain. The maximum temperature in Delhi is expected to be around 34 to 35 degrees Celsius, while the minimum temperature of 23 to 25 degrees Celsius.

. Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has said that Chartered Accountants have a pivotal role in strengthening India-US economic partnership by helping businesses navigate cross-border taxation, regulatory compliance and financial governance, while making Indian enterprises investment-ready for global capital.He said this during an interaction with the leadership and members of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India, from Chicago, Michigan and Ohio Chapters. In a social media post, Mr Goyal said that during the meeting expanding opportunities in the India-US economic partnership were deliberated. He said that India’s economic momentum, marked by strong GDP growth and record foreign direct investment inflows, reflects Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of a confident, self-reliant and globally competitive India.
. Greco Roman wrestler Nitesh Siwach today bagged silver medal in men’s 97kg at Asian games in Japan. Nitesh lost to Japan’s Yuri Nakazato 0-4 in the final.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices extended their losing streak for the fourth straight day today. The Sensex plunged 571 points or 0.8 per cent to close at 71,910. The Nifty shed 199 points or 0.9 per cent to settle at 22,422.In the broader market at the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 as well as the Smallcap 100 indices tumbled one per cent each.

. President Droupadi Murmu has congratulated Kumkum Anil Mohod on scripting history as the first Indian to win the Gold Medal in the Recurve Women’s Individual event at the Asian Games 2026.In a social media post, the President said that Kumkum Anil Mohod had an exceptional campaign at the Games, with two more medals in team events. She said that the athlete has made a major contribution to the superlative success of India’s women archers at this edition of the Asian Games. The President said that her performance and achievements will inspire countless youth, especially girls, to excel in their pursuits.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Andaman and Nicobar Islands, South Interior Karnataka and Uttarakhand tomorrow. It has also predicted thunderstorms accompanied with lightning and gusty winds over North Eastern parts of India, including Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura, during the next two days. According to IMD, Himachal Pradesh, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Maharashtra, Marathwada, Odisha and Telangana are also likely to witness similar weather conditions tomorrow.

. Yemen said its forces carried out 20 strikes against Houthi targets in Taiz province over a three-hour period. The Military spokesperson for Yemen’s internationally recognised government today said the strikes targeted Houthi movements, personnel, vehicles, and military equipment in the province.The escalation follows Saudi Arabia’s announcement that the Iran-backed armed group – Houthis had attacked a power distribution station in Medina yesterday, which supplies electricity to the Prophet’s Mosque.The latest violence marks a significant escalation between Saudi Arabia and the Iran-aligned Houthis, following a UN-brokered truce that largely halted cross-border attacks in 2022.The renewed fighting has already displaced tens of thousands of people and could alter the balance of control in Yemen, with broader implications for maritime security, Red Sea shipping routes, and the strategically important Bab el-Mandeb Strait.

. India’s men’s squash team bagged the bronze medal at the Asian Games 2026 as they lost 1-2 to Malaysia in the semifinal at Aichi-Nagoya in Japan today.The men’s squash team’s bronze came after the Indian women’s team also lost 1-2 to Hong Kong in the semifinal to secure a bronze medal on the same day. The men’s team’s bronze medal in squash took India’s medal tally to five on Day 12 of the Asian Games today. India’s medal tally has risen to 65, including 10 gold, 23 silver and 32 bronze medals. Currently, India is at 8th position.

. India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Bihar, East Madhya Pradesh, East Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, West Bengal and North Eastern parts of the country during the next two days. IMD said that thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds are likely to prevail over Andhra Pradesh, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Bihar, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Odisha, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim tomorrow. Meanwhile, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and Mahe are expected to experience hot and humid weather till 8th of this month.

As the UAE authorities continue their investigation into the circumstances surrounding the flydubai flight incident, they have cautioned against oversimplifying the incident, speculation or premature conclusions before the investigation is completed. At the same time, Captain Smit’s courage and swift response during the incident continues to draw praise from across the UAE.The UAE’s civil aviation regulator, the General Civil Aviation Authority (GCAA) said that investigation into the incident is continuing under approved procedures, with confidentiality and integrity; and in coordination with relevant regional and international authorities. The GCAA said it would not comment on details or claims in circulation that could pre-empt the findings or affect the course of the investigation at this stage. It urged the public to refrain from circulating speculation or unverified information. GCAA commended the courage and swift response of Captain Smit, the crew and passengers.Flydubai Chief Executive Officer Ghaith Al Ghaith said all passengers and crew on board are safe and being cared for. He thanked the captain, the pilots who secured and landed the aircraft, the cabin crew and passengers who assisted during the challenging situation. Flydubai has temporarily suspended its operations to Tel Aviv at the request of the authorities while the investigation continues. He acknowledged that there are many questions about what happened on board FZ1073, saying a full official investigation is underway to establish the facts. He said flydubai is fully supporting the investigation and stressed the importance of allowing the process to take its course.Dr Anwar Gargash, diplomatic adviser to the President of UAE, also praised Captain Smit’s bravery. In a social media post, he said the Indian pilot demonstrated courage and responsibility in confronting what he described as a dangerous terrorist act and a potential disaster. He also cautioned against oversimplifying the incident or promoting conspiracy theories, stressing the need for vigilance and caution in addressing the risks of extremism and terrorism.

. The Supreme Court will tomorrow hear a plea challenging the Centre’s decision to impose a Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on specified UPI person-to-merchant transactions of over 2,000 rupees.Ending nearly six years of fully free UPI payments, the government has introduced a 0.4 per cent fee on transfers of over 2,000 Rs made to merchants through the UPI platform from October 15, while explicitly ring-fencing everyday person-to-person transactions and small payments from any charge. The MDR will be capped at 300 Rs for payments of 75,000 Rs and above.Essential and thin-margin sectors — railways, telecom, insurance, fuel and agricultural inputs — will pay a flat MDR of 5 Rs per transaction above 2,000 Rs.Payments into mutual funds, securities and through stockbrokers and dealers will attract 0.02 per cent MDR, also capped at 300 Rs. Bench of Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana will hear the plea.The Public Interest Litigation (PIL) filed by advocate Anjan Datta has challenged the Centre’s decision. The plea alleged that the levy has been introduced without adequate statutory safeguards, transparency or public consultation.

. The co-pilot accused of assaulting Captain Smit Machchhar has been transferred to Abu Dhabi. The Saudi Press Agency (SPA), quoting an official source at theSaudiMinistry of Interior, reported that both pilots left the country for Abu Dhabi after receiving medical clearance.The Indian Embassy in Abu Dhabi had yesterday informed that Captain Machchhar had been brought to the UAE and was recovering well.As reported by SPA, the aircraft landed safely at Prince Sultan bin Abdulaziz International Airport in Tabuk at 9:45 a.m. on 30th September (Wednesday), with 174 passengers and an eight-member crew, all of whom received necessary logistical and medical assistance. At 5:40 p.m., passengers continued their journey on a replacement flydubai aircraft, while the crew returned to Dubai on a separate flight.The captain and co-pilot were taken to a local hospital for medical evaluation and treatment. Following medical clearance, both pilots departed Saudi Arabia for Abu Dhabi on 1st October (Thursday), accompanied by the UAE security team.According to SPA, preliminary investigations by Saudi authorities, in coordination with a UAE security team, revealed that an altercation occurred in which the co-pilot assaulted the captain, resulting in injuries to both individuals.
